formula.workload: W = min(8, playing minutes / 60 × share(size) × (1 + 2/9 × (physical + vocal))), the playing minutes the running time less its breaks
formula.drainWithin: the work so far A(t) rises at W per playing time; at each break of m minutes A × (1 − 0.25 × min(1, m / 20)); the drain at t is 0.3 × min(1, b × A(t) / F) × (1 − stamina) × g, b the share places to breathe leave (0.7, or 1), F the full; each segment reads the mean of it over its own stretch of the running, integrated exactly
formula.condition: g = 1 + 0.5 × (1 − readiness / 100), readiness the condition at the curtain (readiness at the hour’s fit, as the night’s judgment reads it), 1 at 100 and 1.5 at 0
formula.energyAfter: E = 5 × W × (1 − 0.5 × stamina) × g, taken once at the call; it reads W, the work done, so a break isn’t credited again
formula.call: held for the running time and a 5-minute curtain call
formula.where: src/engine/content/workload.ts (the running times and the coefficients), src/engine/systems/workload.ts (the formula), src/engine/systems/piece.ts (judgePiece reads it), src/engine/systems/school.ts (the calls, the energy)

coefficients.name: share (participation)
coefficients.basis: SLATE’s design: the catalog keeps no lines or entrances. A lead on for most of the evening, a supporting part half of it, a featured part a fifth, a solo piece all of it.

coefficients.name: perLevel (intensity step)
coefficients.basis: From a source: the 2024 Adult Compendium of Physical Activities, an actor on stage 3.0 METs and a dance performance or rehearsal (03010) 5.0 (BODY.met), so the body’s level 3 is taken at 5.0 and each level a third of the way: (5.0/3.0 − 1)/3. The voice’s level takes the same step, SLATE’s design (no MET is published for the voice; the load before counted the two alike). The shape, time at an intensity, is the dose’s (Titze, Švec and Popolo, J Speech Lang Hear Res 2003;46:919–932); its sizes aren’t sourced.

coefficients.name: full (F)
coefficients.basis: SLATE’s design on the old load’s own anchor, worked out not typed: the work done at the curtain of a lead’s ordinary full-length evening (150 minutes with a 20-minute interval, the catalog’s middle running time) in a play of four levels between body and voice, where the old load (0.6 + 0.12 a level) reached 1. About 2.686. A first draft took 3.5, the heaviest lead’s, which left every ordinary lead well short of the drain’s stated most.

coefficients.name: drain (D)
coefficients.basis: PIECE.drain, kept: SLATE’s estimate since 2026-10-12, unchanged.

coefficients.name: recovers
coefficients.basis: SLATE’s design: what an interval of 20 minutes or more gives back of the drain so far, a shorter pause in proportion. No study found measures what an interval restores of an actor’s work.

coefficients.name: condition (G)
coefficients.basis: SLATE’s design: half again of the drain and the energy at no readiness, nothing more at full.

coefficients.name: energy per unit
coefficients.basis: SLATE’s design, balanced so an ordinary lead at half stamina, rested, costs about the 10 a performance took before (Hedda Gabler’s lead 9.5).

coefficients.name: staminaSpares
coefficients.basis: SLATE’s design: full stamina halves the energy, never takes it to nothing (W4).

coefficients.name: cap
coefficients.basis: SLATE’s bound, above every part the catalog holds (3.56 at most, a lead in Julius Caesar), so none is clamped.

coefficients.name: curtainCall
coefficients.basis: SLATE’s 5 minutes, held with the evening.

coefficients.name: assumed interval
coefficients.basis: Where a listing gives an interval and not its length: the length the RSC’s and the Globe’s listings give, SLATE’s reading.

coefficients.name: break placing
coefficients.value: even shares of the playing time
coefficients.basis: SLATE’s placing: the acts’ lengths aren’t kept.

workedExamples.case: A one-act lead: The Bear (OVO, the Roman Theatre, 2025: 55 minutes, no interval), the body 3 and the voice 2, at half stamina and rested (readiness 100)
steps: Playing 55 minutes; a lead is on for 0.75 of it: 41.25 minutes, 0.6875 stage hours.
No break: the work done rises straight to 1.451 at the curtain, 1.451 / 2.686 = 0.540 of the full.
The drain at the curtain’s fall: 0.3 × 0.540 × (1 − 0.5) × 1 = 8.1% off what tiring reaches; across the night 4.05% on average.
The energy after: 5 × 1.451 × (1 − 0.25) × 1 = 5.4. The call holds 55 + 5 = 60 minutes.
workedExamples.before: A whole evening’s load of 1: 15% off at its last movement whatever its length, 10 energy, a 150-minute call.

workedExamples.case: A full-length supporting part: Hedda Gabler (the National Theatre, to March 2017: 160 minutes with a 20-minute interval), the body 1 and the voice 1, at half stamina and rested
steps: Playing 160 − 20 = 140 minutes; a supporting part is on for 0.5 of it: 1.1667 stage hours.
At the interval, 70 minutes in, the work done is 0.843; the interval gives back a quarter: 0.632. By the curtain 0.632 + 0.843 = 1.474, 0.549 of the full.
The drain at the curtain’s fall: 0.3 × 0.549 × 0.5 = 8.2% off; just before the interval 0.3 × (0.843/2.686) × 0.5 = 4.7%, just after it 3.5%.
The energy after: 5 × 1.685 × 0.75 = 6.3, the interval not taking any of it back. The call holds 165 minutes.
workedExamples.before: A load of 0.84, the same as Hedda’s: 12.6% off at the last movement, 10 energy, 150 minutes.

workedExamples.case: A long, intense lead with an interval: Julius Caesar (Shakespeare’s Globe, 2022: 150 minutes with a 15-minute interval), the body 2 and the voice 3, at half stamina and rested
steps: Playing 135 minutes; a lead 0.75 of it: 1.6875 stage hours.

At the interval, 67.5 minutes in, 1.781 done; a 15-minute interval gives back 0.25 × 15/20 = 0.1875 of it: 1.447. It reaches the full, 2.686, 47 minutes after the interval, and holds there the last 20 minutes.
The drain at the curtain’s fall: 0.3 × 1 × 0.5 = 15% off (30% at no stamina, none at full; 17.3% coming in at readiness 70).
The energy after: 5 × 3.563 × 0.75 = 13.4 (8.9 at full stamina, 17.8 at none, 15.4 at readiness 70). The call holds 155 minutes.
workedExamples.before: A load of 1: 15% off at its last movement, 10 energy, 150 minutes at the School.
